newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle Monday seen priced $70 -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle Monday seen priced $70 -trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early next week were seen priced at $70.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from this week's sales, amid outlooks for tighter cattle supplies, feedlot sources said.
Aggressive marketings have left most feedlots extremely current, with cattle pulled forward as much as two to three weeks ahead of projected marketings, several sources said.

Showlists next week were seen steady to smaller, they said. Lower cattle weights reflected the active marketings, with average weights this week pegged at 1,156 lbs, compared with 1,160 last week and 1,160 last year, USDA reported.
Fed cattle prices were underpinned by strong beef demand earlier in the week, with most of this week's showlists sold on Tuesday, they said.
However, large slaughter this week, along with slower retail buying for Memorial Day meat features, pulled beef prices lower, the dealers said.
Beef production this week was estimated up 4.6 percent from a week ago and down 1.6 percent from a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
